verdict.rationale: Superpowers ships a first-party `writing-skills` meta-skill that guides the agent through authoring skills with a TDD loop. The loop is: write pressure-scenario tests, watch them fail, write the skill, watch tests pass, then refactor to close loopholes, which covers both writing and improving. Packaging guidance is only glimpsed through a note on cross-runtime skill directories. Missing for 10: documented guidance on packaging or distributing new skills (manifest/plugin bundling), and independent hands-on corroboration of the writing-skills workflow.

support.subject: As a developer, the collection ships a meta-skill or tool that guides my agent through writing, improving, and packaging new skills

citations.quote: You write test cases (pressure scenarios with subagents), watch them fail (baseline behavior), write the skill (documentation), watch tests pass (agents comply), and refactor (close loopholes).
The writing-skills module teaches you to author and test new skills
Writing skills IS Test-Driven Development applied to process documentation.
Codex, Copilot CLI, and Gemini CLI all also recognize `~/.agents/skills/` as a cross-runtime alias.
